mainTopic: חזקה and רוב in רבי מאיר's rulings, how long a woman waits before חליצה, and two sisters-in-law who testify about their husbands' deaths
overview: The גמרא first finishes explaining why רבי מאיר is strict in the רישא of the משנה but lenient in the סיפא. In the רישא, the חזקה and the minority of women who miscarry together balance the רוב, so the woman can neither marry nor do יבום. In the סיפא, the חזקה and the רוב agree, and a brother being born is only a minority of a minority, which even רבי מאיר ignores. The גמרא then asks whether the woman in the רישא must wait forever. זעירי says she waits nine months and then does חליצה, which works either way. רבי חנינא says she must wait until the facts are known, because an unneeded חליצה would require an announcement that she may still marry a כהן. Some people would miss that announcement. The גמרא tests this reasoning against an earlier משנה and answers it in two ways. A new משנה follows, about two sisters-in-law who each say their husband died, and a ברייתא adds a case. The amud ends with רבא asking for the reason behind רבי אלעזר's leniency, and the גמרא asks what practical difference his two options make.

steps.title: In the first case, the presumption and the majority point in opposite directions
steps.stepSummary: In the רישא, the חזקה says the woman needs יבום, but the רוב says she is free to marry. A חזקה is weaker than a רוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the first clause, the presumption points to levirate marriage, and the majority points to marrying anyone. A presumption is not stronger than a majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the רישא by setting up a conflict between two kinds of evidence. This step only lays out the problem; the next step finishes the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her husband was last known to have no children, so the חזקה is that she needs יבום. But most women do have children, so the רוב says the צרה probably had a child, which would free her. Since a רוב normally beats a חזקה, we would expect her to be allowed to marry right away. That is the puzzle the next step solves.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of the משנה
A presumption that things stay as they were last known
Levirate marriage to the husband's brother
Literally 'to the market'; free to marry any man

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two women. The woman in the רישא is the wife who stayed home. The one who may be pregnant is her צרה, who went overseas with the husband.

phrases.english: The first clause: the presumption is toward levirate marriage,
phrases.notes: When the husband left, he had no children, so we presume he died without any.

phrases.english: and the majority is toward the market (marrying anyone).
phrases.notes: Most women give birth, so the צרה probably had a child, which would free this woman.

phrases.english: And a presumption is not as strong as a majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an answer begun before this section, explaining why רבי מאיר rules the way he does in the רישא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a רוב beats a חזקה, she should be allowed to marry anyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: This is resolved in the next step.

steps.title: Women who miscarry tip the balance to an even split
steps.stepSummary: The minority of women who miscarry is added to the side of the חזקה, so both sides become equal. That is why she can neither marry nor do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bring the minority of women who miscarry and join it to the presumption. Then it is half and half, so she may not marry anyone and may not do levirate marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining the רישא. Adding the women who miscarry to the חזקה makes the two sides equal, so the woman is stuck in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some women who become pregnant miscarry, and a miscarriage does not free the widow. That small group backs up the חזקה that there is no child. Together they balance out the רוב, leaving a true 50/50 doubt, so we are strict in both directions.

keyTerms.meaning: A minority; what happens less often
Half and half; an even doubt

steps.whatToRemember: In the רישא, the חזקה plus the minority who miscarry equal the רוב, so it is a full doubt. She may not marry anyone, and she may not do יבום.

phrases.english: But bring the minority of women who miscarry
and join it to the presumption,
and it becomes half and half —
so she shall not marry, and she shall not enter levirate marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the puzzle raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Joining a minority to a חזקה to cancel out a רוב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רוב should win, and she should be free to marry.
steps.terutzMaskana: The minority who miscarry plus the חזקה equal the רוב, so the doubt leads to strictness both ways.

steps.title: In the second case, the presumption and the majority agree
steps.stepSummary: In the סיפא, both the חזקה and the רוב say she is free to marry. A living brother would be only a tiny minority, and even רבי מאיר does not worry about that.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the latter clause, the presumption is toward marrying anyone, and the majority is also toward marrying anyone. Males are a minority of a minority, and רבי מאיר is not concerned about a minority of a minority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the סיפא is lenient. Both kinds of evidence point the same way, and the opposing chance is tiny.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her husband had no brother when the mother-in-law left, so the חזקה is that she is free. A living baby boy being born is also not the usual outcome, so the רוב agrees. The chance of a brother is too small to count, even for רבי מאיר, who usually does worry about a minority.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of the משנה
Males; here, a baby brother who would require יבום
A minority of a minority; a very small chance

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר does worry about a minority, but not about a 'minority of a minority.' When the חזקה and the רוב agree, the tiny other side is ignored.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the limit of רבי מאיר's well-known concern for a מיעוט. It explains how he can be strict in the רישא and lenient in the סיפא without contradicting himself.

phrases.english: The latter clause: the presumption is toward the market,
phrases.notes: When the mother-in-law left, the husband had no brother, so we presume he still has none.

phrases.english: and the majority is also toward the market.
So males are a minority of a minority,
phrases.notes: For a brother to exist, she must have had a living baby, and it must be a boy. Each step makes the chance smaller.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִיעוּטָא דְמִיעוּטָא — לָא חָיֵישׁ רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: and about a minority of a minority, רבי מאיר is not concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the סיפא with the רישא explained in steps 1 and 2, completing the answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: חזקה against רוב compared with חזקה together with רוב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר worries about a minority, so he should be strict in the סיפא too.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the סיפא the opposing chance is only a minority of a minority, which even רבי מאיר ignores.

steps.title: Must she wait forever?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that she can neither marry nor do יבום, and asks whether that means she is stuck forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'She shall not marry and shall not enter levirate marriage,' and so on. Forever?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and challenges it. Surely she cannot be left unable to marry for the rest of her life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's wording sounds open-ended, as if she is chained with no way out. The גמרא pushes back, since there should be a way to settle her status. This sets up זעירי's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And so on'; the rest of the quote from the משנה

phrases.english: 'She shall not marry and shall not enter levirate marriage,' etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the רישא of the משנה, the case explained in steps 1 and 2.

phrases.english: And forever?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא תִּנָּשֵׂא וְלֹא תִּתְיַיבֵּם וְכוּ׳. וּלְעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רישא/סיפא discussion and asks about how long the רישא's ruling lasts.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's open-ended ruling that she may neither marry nor do יבום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leaving a woman unable to marry forever makes no sense when there is a way to settle the doubt.

steps.title: זעירי: wait nine months, then do חליצה to cover both possibilities
steps.stepSummary: זעירי explains that she waits three months for her own sake and nine months because of her צרה. Then she does חליצה, which works whichever way things turned out.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said: for her own sake, three months; for her fellow wife's sake, nine months. Then she does חליצה either way.
steps.whatsHappening: זעירי answers the challenge. She does not wait forever, only nine months, and then חליצה frees her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every widow waits three months before remarrying. Here she must wait nine months, until it is clear whether the צרה was pregnant, because חליצה done while a wife is pregnant does not work. After nine months, חליצה covers both sides: if there was a child it was not needed, and if there was no child it releases her from יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: For herself; the wait every widow keeps
For her fellow wife; because the צרה may be pregnant
Whichever way you look at it; covers both possibilities

steps.whatToRemember: According to זעירי, the woman in the רישא waits nine months and then does חליצה, which works either way. After that she may marry anyone. The next step brings רבי חנינא, who disagrees.

phrases.english: זעירי said:
For herself: three months,
for her fellow wife: nine,
phrases.notes: Nine months is enough time for the צרה to give birth if she was pregnant.

phrases.english: and she performs חליצה whichever way it turned out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setting a time limit and a solution that works either way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to leave her unable to marry forever.
steps.terutzMaskana: She waits nine months, does חליצה to cover both possibilities, and is then free to marry.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wait three months for herself and nine for her צרה, then do חליצה to cover both possibilities.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: three months for herself, indefinitely for her co-wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא disagrees with זעירי. For her own possible pregnancy she waits three months, but for her צרה's possible child she must wait until the facts are known.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: For her own sake, she waits three months. For her co-wife's sake, she waits forever.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer to how long this woman must wait. רבי חנינא splits the two worries and treats them differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like זעירי, he says three months covers the worry that she herself is pregnant. But for the worry that her צרה had a child, he does not let her do חליצה after nine months. She must wait until we actually find out what happened with the צרה.

keyTerms.meaning: For herself, meaning the worry that she herself is pregnant
For her fellow wife, meaning the worry about her צרה's child
Forever, meaning until the facts become known

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
For herself, three [months];
for her fellow wife, forever.
phrases.notes: "Her fellow wife" is her צרה, her husband's other wife. "Forever" means until we find out whether the צרה had a child.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer, different from זעירי's, to the question of how long she must wait.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She waits three months because of her own possible pregnancy, and indefinitely because of her צרה, until the facts are known.

steps.title: Why not let her do חליצה, which works either way?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא: after nine months, חליצה covers every possibility, so why make her wait forever?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let her do חליצה, since it works whichever way things turned out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי חנינא, using the very argument זעירי used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the צרה had no living child, this woman needs חליצה. If the צרה did have a child, she needs nothing at all. Either way, doing חליצה seems to cause no harm, so there should be no reason to leave her stuck forever.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it, since it works in either case

phrases.english: But let her do chalitza whichever way you look at it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי חנינא's ruling in step 6, using זעירי's reasoning from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's ruling that she waits indefinitely for her צרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חליצה is a safe option in every case, so waiting forever seems pointless.

steps.title: An unneeded חליצה would require an announcement for the כהונה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים decreed against חליצה here. If the צרה did have a living child, the חליצה was not needed, and we would have to announce that this woman is still allowed to marry a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי בר אבין and רבי חנינא בר אבין both said: It is a decree, in case there turns out to be a living child. Then you would end up needing to make an announcement that she is allowed to marry into the כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים explain why רבי חנינא does not allow חליצה. They point to a hidden downside of doing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a חלוצה may not marry a כהן. But if the צרה really had a living child, this woman was never bound to יבום, so her חליצה means nothing and she is still allowed to a כהן. The חכמים did not want to create a situation that needs a public announcement to fix it.

keyTerms.meaning: A decree, a protective rule made by the חכמים
A child who lives, a viable child
The priesthood, meaning being allowed to marry a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that the חליצה forbids her to a כהן by mistake. If the צרה had a living child, the חליצה does not count, so she stays allowed to a כהן. The trouble is that people need to be told this.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר אָבִין
phrases.english: Abaye bar Avin and Rabbi Chanina bar Avin

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יְהֵא וָלָד בֶּן קַיָּימָא,
phrases.english: both say: It is a decree, lest there be a viable child,
phrases.notes: This means a living child of the צרה. Then this woman never needed יבום or חליצה at all.

phrases.english: and you would end up requiring an announcement for her regarding the priesthood.
phrases.notes: The announcement would tell everyone that she may still marry a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר אָבִין אָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ גְּזֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by showing that חליצה is not completely harmless.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a hidden downside of the seemingly safe option
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חליצה seemed to have no downside in any possible case.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the צרה had a living child, the חליצה would be meaningless and would require a public announcement that she may marry a כהן. So the חכמים decreed against it.

steps.title: So let them make the announcement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why that is a problem. If it turns out that the צרה had a child, just make the announcement.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let her need an announcement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. An announcement does not sound like a big deal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making an announcement is easy. That hardly seems a good enough reason to leave a woman unable to marry forever.

keyTerms.meaning: So let her need it, meaning let the announcement be made

phrases.english: So let her need [an announcement]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that needing an announcement is a reason to forbid חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An announcement is a simple fix, so it should not be a reason to leave the woman stuck.

steps.title: People who saw the חליצה may miss the announcement
steps.stepSummary: Some people will be at the חליצה but not hear the announcement. Then they will think a חלוצה is being allowed to marry a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps there will be people who were at the חליצה but not at the announcement. They will say: They have allowed a חלוצה to marry a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why an announcement does not fully solve the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The public saw a חליצה happen. Not everyone will hear the later correction. Those people will see her marry a כהן and conclude that the חכמים allow a חלוצה to a כהן, which is a dangerous mistake. That is the reason for the decree.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who has done חליצה, who is forbidden to a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא forbids חליצה because a pointless חליצה could lead people to think a חלוצה may marry a כהן. An announcement will not reach everyone who saw the חליצה.

phrases.english: Perhaps there are those who were at the chalitza
but were not at the announcement,
and they will say: They permitted a chalutza to a kohen.
phrases.notes: "קשרו" literally means "they tied," and here it means "they allowed."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא אִיכָּא דְּהָוֵי בַּחֲלִיצָה וְלָא הָוֵי בְּהַכְרָזָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9's challenge and supports the reasoning of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An announcement would easily fix things.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not everyone who saw the חליצה will hear the announcement, so people may think a חלוצה may marry a כהן.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about a son born overseas
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה where a woman claims her husband died before her son. She is not believed, but we still worry about her words, so she does חליצה and not יבום, even though by her own claim the חליצה might be unneeded.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: A woman says, "A son was born to me overseas." If she said, "My son died and then my husband died," she is believed. If she said, "My husband died and then my son died," she is not believed. Still, we worry about her words, so she does חליצה and not יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to set up a challenge to what was just said. The actual question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her claim is true, her husband left a living son when he died, so she owes no יבום or חליצה at all. In that case the חליצה is meaningless and she stays allowed to a כהן, which is exactly the situation the decree feared. Yet the משנה requires חליצה anyway, which seems to go against אביי בר אבין and רבי חנינא בר אבין.

keyTerms.meaning: We take her words into account

steps.confusionAlert: "Not believed" and "we worry about her words" are two separate things. Her claim is not strong enough to free her without חליצה, but it is strong enough to stop יבום.

phrases.english: We learned: "A son was born to me overseas,"

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרָה: ״מֵת בְּנִי וְאַחַר כָּךְ בַּעְלִי״ — נֶאֱמֶנֶת.
phrases.english: and she said: "My son died and then my husband"—she is believed.

phrases.aramaic: ״מֵת בַּעְלִי וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּנִי״ — אֵינָהּ נֶאֱמֶנֶת,
phrases.english: "My husband died and then my son"—she is not believed,
but we are concerned for her words,
so she does chalitza and does not do yibum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to test the decree described in steps 8 and 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decree that we avoid a possibly unneeded חליצה because of the announcement problem
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In this משנה the חליצה may also be unneeded, yet the משנה requires it and does not worry about the announcement.

steps.title: Witnesses might later confirm her story
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge from the earlier משנה. Witnesses might later confirm the woman's claim, which would make her חליצה unneeded and force a כרוז לכהונה. Yet the משנה still has her do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we should worry that witnesses might come and say exactly what she said, and then you would need to make an announcement that she may marry a כהן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing the question it began in step 11. The earlier משנה does not seem to worry about needing a כרוז, which goes against the reason given in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If witnesses later confirm that her husband died first, while her son was still alive, then she never needed יבום or חליצה at all. We would then have to announce that she may still marry a כהן. Since the משנה still requires חליצה, the כרוז worry seems not to matter, and that weakens the answer given for רבי חנינא.

keyTerms.meaning: The priesthood, meaning marriage to a כהן

phrases.english: But let us worry that perhaps witnesses will come
and say just as she said,
phrases.notes: Her claim was that her husband died first, and then her son died.

phrases.english: and it turns out that you require an announcement for her about marrying a כהן!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 8 (defended in step 10) that חליצה is avoided so that a כרוז will not be needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The earlier משנה requires חליצה even though a כרוז might later be needed, so the כרוז worry should not stop חליצה in רבי חנינא's case either.

steps.title: רב פפא: she was a divorcee
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the earlier משנה is about a woman who was once divorced. She is already forbidden to a כהן, so no כרוז would ever be needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The case is of a divorced woman.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge. He limits the earlier משנה to a woman who is already a גרושה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גרושה is forbidden to a כהן no matter what. So even if her חליצה turns out to be unneeded, there is nothing to announce. The כרוז worry never comes up in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: A divorced woman, forbidden to marry a כהן

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is about a divorced woman.
phrases.notes: She was divorced from an earlier husband, so she could never marry a כהן anyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier משנה ignores the כרוז worry.
steps.terutzMaskana: The earlier משנה is about a woman for whom no כרוז is ever relevant.

steps.title: רב חייא: they hid alone in a cave
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בריה דרב הונא answers that she claimed she and her husband hid in a cave. No one else saw what happened, so witnesses can never come.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא son of רב הונא said: The case is where she said, 'He and I were hiding in a cave.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to the same challenge. Here the woman's story itself rules out any witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that witnesses might later confirm her story. If the events happened in a hidden cave, nobody else could testify. So no כרוז will ever be needed.
steps.whatToRemember: Both answers keep the rule from step 8, that חליצה is avoided where it might later force a כרוז. They show that the earlier משנה is a case where no כרוז could ever be needed.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא אָמַר,
phrases.english: Rav Chiya son of Rav Huna said:
It is where she said: 'He and I were hiding in a cave.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Witnesses might later confirm her claim.
steps.terutzMaskana: In her case no witnesses could exist, so a כרוז would never be needed.

steps.title: Two sisters-in-law each say their husband died
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. Two יבמות each say that their own husband died. Each one is forbidden to remarry because of the other's husband, who would be her יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Two sisters-in-law. This one says 'My husband died,' and that one says 'My husband died.' This one is forbidden because of that one's husband, and that one is forbidden because of this one's husband.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It deals with two women married to two brothers who had no children, and each woman reports her own husband's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each woman is believed about her own husband, but she is not believed about her sister-in-law's husband. That brother is her יבם, so maybe he is still alive and she still needs יבום or חליצה. So both women stay forbidden to marry.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden, here meaning forbidden to marry someone else

steps.confusionAlert: 'Forbidden because of her husband' does not mean the other woman's own husband forbids her. It means the other woman's husband is this woman's יבם, and he might still be alive.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Two sisters-in-law,
phrases.notes: They are married to two brothers, and both brothers left with no children.

phrases.english: this one says: 'My husband died,'
and that one says: 'My husband died.'

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ אֲסוּרָה מִפְּנֵי בַּעְלָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ,
phrases.english: This one is forbidden because of that one's husband,

phrases.aramaic: וְזוֹ אֲסוּרָה מִפְּנֵי בַּעְלָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ.
phrases.english: and that one is forbidden because of this one's husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה, unrelated to the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יבמה is not believed about her sister-in-law's husband, so each woman stays forbidden until her יבם is known to be dead.

steps.title: When only one woman has witnesses
steps.stepSummary: If one woman has witnesses to her husband's death, she stays forbidden. The one without witnesses is allowed to remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: If this one has witnesses and that one has no witnesses, the one with witnesses is forbidden and the one without witnesses is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a case where only one husband's death is confirmed by witnesses. The result is the opposite of what we might expect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman without witnesses is believed about her own husband. The witnesses confirm her יבם died, so she is fully free. The woman with witnesses has nobody reliable about her יבם, only her sister-in-law's word, so she stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted, here meaning allowed to remarry

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the woman with witnesses is better off. Her own husband's death is proven, but her יבם's death is not, so she is the one who stays forbidden.

phrases.english: If this one has witnesses and that one has no witnesses,
the one who has witnesses is forbidden,
and the one who has no witnesses is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a variation to the basic case of step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: What frees a woman is proof about her יבם, not proof about her own husband.

steps.title: When only one woman has children
steps.stepSummary: The woman with children may remarry. The woman without children stays forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If this one has children and that one has no children, the one with children is permitted and the one without children is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: Another variation: one woman has children from her husband and the other does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman with children is believed about her own husband, and her children free her from יבום, so she may remarry. The woman without children still needs her יבם to be dead. Only her sister-in-law says he died, so she stays forbidden.

phrases.english: If this one has children and that one has no children,
the one who has children is permitted,
and the one who has no children is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further variation on the case of step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman with children needs no יבום, so her own word about her husband is enough to free her.

steps.title: After יבום, when the יבמין died
steps.stepSummary: The women married other brothers through יבום, and then those brothers died. The תנא קמא says the women are still forbidden to marry.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they did יבום and the יבמין died, they are forbidden to marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a case where each woman did יבום with another brother, and he then died with no children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original worry has not gone away: the other woman's husband might still be alive as a יבם. So the תנא קמא keeps both women forbidden to marry anyone else.

phrases.english: If they did יבום, and the יבמין died,
phrases.notes: These are other brothers in the family, not the two husbands the women said had died.

phrases.english: they are forbidden to marry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a case after יבום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The worry about a living יבם stays even after יבום with another brother.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: permitted to the יבמין means permitted to all
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר disagrees. Since the women were allowed to marry the יבמין, they are allowed to marry anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: Since they were permitted to the יבמין, they are permitted to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר argues on the ruling in step 18. With this disagreement the משנה ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each woman was trusted enough to do יבום on the basis of her own word. רבי אלעזר says that trust carries over, so once the יבמין die, the women may marry anyone. The תנא קמא does not extend it that way.
steps.whatToRemember: In this משנה, a יבמה is believed about her own husband but not about her sister-in-law's husband. רבי אלעזר holds that once she was allowed to the יבמין, she is allowed to everyone.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
Since they were permitted to the יבמין,
they are permitted to every man.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: הוֹאִיל וְהוּתְּרוּ לַיְּבָמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling of step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being permitted to the יבמין makes the women permitted to everyone.

steps.title: Witnesses and children: both women may remarry
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if one woman has witnesses and children and the other has neither, both may remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: if one woman has witnesses and children, and the other has no witnesses and no children, both are permitted to remarry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ברייתא that adds a new case to the משנה. In this case, both women end up allowed to remarry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman with children is exempt from יבום, and witnesses confirm her husband died, so she is free. Her husband was the other woman's יבם. The witnesses prove he is dead, so nothing holds back the second woman either. That is why she is free too, even though she has no witnesses or children of her own.

keyTerms.meaning: Children (which exempt a widow from יבום)

steps.confusionAlert: The witnesses help both women. They prove that the first woman's husband died, and that same man was the second woman's יבם.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
If this one has witnesses and children,
and that one has neither witnesses nor children —
they are both permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a combined case to the משנה's cases of witnesses (step 16) and children (step 17).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one woman has both witnesses and children, both women may remarry.

steps.title: The משנה's argument after יבום, quoted again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה again: after יבום and the death of the יבמין, the תנא קמא forbids remarriage, but רבי אלעזר permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they did יבום and the יבמין died, they are forbidden to remarry. רבי אלעזר says: since they were permitted to the יבמין, they are permitted to anyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the line of the משנה that it now wants to discuss. This step sets up רבא's question about רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is ruled here. The גמרא quotes the argument from steps 18-19 again so that it can look into the reason behind רבי אלעזר's leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: The brothers-in-law who did the יבום

phrases.english: If they did יבום and the יבמין died —
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's line from steps 18-19, quoted again so the גמרא can discuss it.

phrases.english: they are forbidden to marry.
Rabbi Elazar says:
Since they were permitted to the יבמין —
they are permitted to anyone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא back to the משנה's argument, to discuss it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: forbidden to remarry. רבי אלעזר: permitted to anyone.

steps.title: רבא asks why רבי אלעזר permits them
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether רבי אלעזר's reason is that a צרה can testify for the other woman, or that a woman would not harm herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: What is רבי אלעזר's reason? Is it because he holds that a צרה may testify for her fellow? Or perhaps it is because she would not harm herself?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a question with two possible answers. He wants to know what reason lies behind רבי אלעזר's leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option 1: רבי אלעזר simply holds that women like these, who normally are not trusted about each other, are believed after all. Option 2: they are believed here only because each woman did יבום herself. If her own husband were really alive, she would be living in a forbidden relationship, so we can be sure she was telling the truth.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raised a question with possible answers)
A co-wife, normally not trusted to testify about the other wife

steps.whyThisMatters: The two reasons lead to different rules. One says these women are trusted in general. The other says they are trusted only when the woman's own behavior backs up her word.

phrases.english: Rava asked:
What is Rabbi Elazar's reason?
Is it because he holds
that a rival wife may testify for her fellow,
phrases.notes: These two women are not co-wives, but like a צרה, they are a pair who normally are not trusted about each other.

phrases.english: or perhaps it is because
she would not ruin herself.
phrases.notes: She did יבום herself. If her husband were alive, that would be a forbidden relationship, so she would not lie about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks into the reason behind רבי אלעזר's view, which was just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אלעזר's leniency comes from trusting a צרה in general, or from the woman's own act of יבום proving she is telling the truth.

steps.title: What difference do the two reasons make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רבא's two possible reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks in which case the two reasons would lead to different results. This step sets up the next move, where a case will be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before trying to decide between the two reasons, the גמרא wants to see a case where they actually lead to different rulings.

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבא's two options by asking where they would lead to different rulings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two reasons for רבי אלעזר's view lead to different rulings.
